translate_en|mods/TrueCompanions/42/medi: Multiplier on affinity / affection changes from conversation and quests. 1.0 = default.

When ON, a recruited companion that gets bitten builds up infection and eventually TURNS into a zombie, permanently - for players who want that risk. When OFF (default), companions never zombify. Either way, the false zombification bug (companion turning after a reload for no reason) is always prevented.
Companions close doors behind them at base
When on, a companion who opens a door inside a base area pulls it shut once she is clear of it. Only simple single-leaf doors; double and garage doors are never touched.

When ON, a following companion hops into your vehicle when you drive off (they board and are safely stowed - not physically seated) and step out next to you when you exit. Works with modded vehicles. This does not require the Bandits mod's own 'may enter vehicles' checkbox.

Writes a detailed record of what every companion decides and does to TrueCompanions_trace.txt in the Lua sub-folder of your Zomboid folder (the same place as your saves and Logs). Leave this OFF for normal play - it costs performance and the file grows steadily. Turn it ON only when you are reproducing a bug on purpose, then send the file with your report: it is the difference between a guess and an answer.

ON by default. When a companion holds a walk order but has not moved for about nine seconds her task queue is cleared to force a fresh path, and at about twenty seconds she is stepped directly to her destination. This is what stops a companion standing against a wall forever. Turn it OFF only while bug-hunting: if she still freezes with this off, the freeze is real and the watchdog was only reacting to it - if instead she frees herself, the watchdog was making things worse.

When ON, a recruited companion that would die is instead KNOCKED DOWN - it lies incapacitated until you open the V window and press 'Help up companion'. They still take damage, bleed, and get hungry/tired. Turn OFF for normal mortality (they can die for good). Zombification is a separate option below.

When ON, a companion carrying a firearm never runs out: their reserve is quietly topped up so they keep reloading without you handing over magazines. When OFF (default), they only fire what you actually give them.

Show a real head-and-shoulders 3D render of the NPC's face in the V window's profile tab and in conversation. EXPERIMENTAL - this uses the engine's character model widget, which had GPU trouble in an earlier build; test it before relying on it. Off = no portrait.
A need at or above this value makes the companion break off to take care of it (if a matching routine spot is assigned).
How fast companion Hunger / Fatigue / Boredom / Hygiene rise. 1.0 = default, 0 = needs never rise.
When on, neutral wanderers stop and face you when you stand close, so you can talk before they move on.
When on, the player cannot hurt or kill a recruited companion.

If PZ's save/load loses a recruited companion, bring it back at its post (Stay tile / Guard spot / where it was). EXPERIMENTAL - it respawns the companion from a saved roster; test it on a backup save first. Off = no auto-restore (duplicates are still cleaned up regardless).
Scales the companion dialog/UI window and its text. 1.0 = default. Raise it if the UI looks too small on a high-resolution screen (e.g. 1.25 or 1.5). Reopen the window after changing.
Spawning pauses while at least this many un-recruited neutral survivors are already near you (a LOCAL throttle, not a total limit - explore and you'll keep finding more). 0 = no throttle.

Spawn recruitable companions ONLY from the clan(s) you name here. Enter the clan's name EXACTLY as it appears in the Bandit Creator (the 'Name' field shown when you create or edit a clan, e.g. Survivors). For more than one clan, separate names with commas: Survivors, Recon. Leave EMPTY to use any friendly/companion clan. Names are case-insensitive. (A clickable clan checklist is also available in-game: right-click the ground -> NPC Core Editor -> Spawning tab.)
How often a lone neutral survivor (recruitable) wanders into the area off-screen. Base Bandits almost never spawns friendly groups, so this fills that gap. Off disables it.

"Forget growing it -- it's about not wasting it. A root cellar, some salt, and I can stretch one deer through a whole winter. Find the food; I'll make it last."
"Follow the deer. Where they graze, the land's still good. There's an orchard gone wild south of the farms -- apples for the taking if the bears don't beat you to it."
"You don't need a farm -- you need a snare line and patience. Set traps along the game trails by the creek and you'll never go hungry. I'll show you the spots."

"I wore the uniform. The Knox facility wasn't a containment site -- it was a research lab. They knew weeks before they warned anyone. We were ordered to hold a line we were never told the truth about."
"I scouted that perimeter before the fences went up. Heavy vehicles, comms towers, men who didn't answer questions. Whatever this is, it started behind those gates."
"That forest bunker's no myth -- I've stood on its hatch. Concealed entry off an old logging trail northeast of the lake. Whether anyone's still home is another question."
"Safest place is wherever the herds aren't, and that changes daily. But the deep woods past the ridge? They don't wander up there. I'd build there if I were settling down."
"Find me an onion and a little heat and I'll make you forget it's the end of the world. For one plate, anyway."
"Give me a generator, some fuel, and ten minutes where nothing's trying to eat me. Hot showers again -- imagine that."
"You treat the clutch like it owes you money. But you keep us moving, so I'll allow it."
"Every time you grind the gears, a little piece of me dies. Otherwise? Not bad."
"That scratch says otherwise. Sit. Let me look before it turns -- they ALL turn now."
"'Fine' is what people say right before they spike a fever. Humor me and roll up your sleeve."
"Spent years where the only map was the sky and the moss on the trees. Towns turn me around. The wild never does."
"No. I don't. Some doors you don't open out here. Just know I'm good in a fight, and leave it at that."
"Ha. Relax. Old habits, sure -- but I don't steal from the people who watch my back. ...Probably."
"Rabbit, mostly. Fat one yesterday. Out here a snare line beats a gun -- quiet, and it works while you sleep."
"I'm not your dog. Watch your tone with me."
"With you? Maybe. For the first time, I think maybe."
"That's rich, coming from you. Fine. Whatever you say, boss."
"...I feel the same. Have for a while now."
"...wow. Noted. I'll keep my feelings to myself from now on, then. Lesson learned."
"...you didn't deny it. I don't know whether to be grateful you're honest or furious you did it. Both, probably."
"I won't ask you to choose -- the world's too small and cruel for that. Just don't make me feel like a fool."
"...words are cheap, but I want to believe you. So don't make a liar of me. Please."
"Heh. That was awful. I needed it."
"Heat, timing, and never wasting a scrap. Pay attention."
"Rule one: assume every wire is live and wants you dead. Now, slowly..."
"Alright. Breathe out when you swing, don't flail, and never back into a corner. Again."
"Pop the hood. A car's just a thousand small problems that trust each other. Here."
"Sit. First rule: stop the bleeding, then worry about the pain. Watch my hands."
"...wow. I'm doing my best out here, same as you."
"Charming. Want to trade packs and find out how heavy it is?"
"...about time. Don't let go, alright? Not tonight."
"Every single day. That's why I watch your back like I do. Don't you dare die on me."
"A house with a door that locks for the right reasons. A garden. You, complaining about my cooking. That's the whole dream."
"Quiet. Just quiet, and you next to me. I stopped wanting more than that a long time ago."
"...I love you too. Saying it feels dangerous, like it can be taken away. But it's true."
"...I've noticed. I don't mind. Bit of warmth in all this -- I'll take it."
"Yeah? And here I thought I was being subtle about watching you back."
"...then don't. I'm tired of pretending too. Whatever this is -- I want it."
"You and me. To the end of it. I'm not going anywhere -- you're stuck with me now."
"...I was hoping you'd say that. Yes. Whatever this is -- let's find out together."
"...oh. Right. No, I get it. Friends, then -- I'd rather have that than lose you."
"A school. I won't describe it. Just... don't go to the one off the highway. Promise me."
"They move different at night. In packs. Almost like they remember how to hunt. I don't sleep much."
"The farms out past the treeline. Animals gone feral, fields gone wild, but a smart forager eats like a king out there."
"McCoy land had logging cabins with stocked larders. Far from the roads. Far from help, too."
"Warehouses down by the river. Everyone hit the pharmacies first -- nobody thinks about the loading docks."
"The gun store in town was stripped day one. But the houses behind it? People left in a hurry. Doors still unlocked."
"The big city? They walled it and it didn't matter. Millions behind that concrete. If you go in, you don't come out -- but the mall never got picked clean..."
"Louisville's a graveyard the size of a county. Army dropped the bridges to slow them. Whatever's behind the wall is still in there, pacing."
"March Ridge, maybe. Small, fenced. There were army trailers parked at the south end before the end -- supplies, if the looters left any."
"The Knox facility up north was ground zero. Whole region got sealed off -- nobody who went to look came back."
"There was a checkpoint on the bridge to West Point. By the end they were turning survivors away at gunpoint."
"Muldraugh's a one-road town -- gas station, warehouses, a sawmill. The horde rolls down Main Street like a tide. Loot the edges, never the middle."
"There's a storage lot in Muldraugh nobody bothered with. Padlocks, mostly. If you've got a sledge and nerve, might be worth it."
"Riverside's quieter -- rich little river town. Big houses, full pantries, folks who locked up tight and never made it back. Watch the gated streets."
"People whispered about a prepper's bunker out in the forest. Could be a myth -- could be the last dry bed in the county."
"The Rosewood fire station had a solid setup before it got overrun. Might still be worth a look, if you're brave."
"A looping emergency message, mostly. But one night I swear I heard a real voice -- a woman, giving coordinates. Then static. I've wondered ever since."
"The official channels went dead weeks ago. Anything you hear now is either a recording... or someone who shouldn't still be out there talking."
"West Point's got everything and ten thousand of them to guard it. The pharmacy and the gun store are gold -- if you can stand the noise you'll make getting out."
What I'd give for a real meal.
Think you could get us some power?

I love you. I needed to say it out loud.
I catch myself watching you sometimes.
I don't want to pretend this is just survival.
